title: Erdős Problem #1065: Primes of the Form 2^k · q + 1
description: Are there infinitely many primes p = 2^k · q + 1 (q prime, k ≥ 0)? More generally, p = 2^k · 3^l · q + 1? Connected to safe primes and smooth-minus-one primes. OEIS A074781, A339465.

references: Guy B46: Unsolved Problems in Number Theory
OEIS A074781: primes p with (p−1)/2 prime
Hardy–Littlewood (1923): Conjectures on prime constellations and safe primes density
Artin (1927): Primitive root conjecture (related via factorization of p−1)
Pomerance (1980): Popular values of Euler's function (smooth shifted primes)

crossReferences.description: Safe primes (p = 2q + 1) are the k=1 special case of Form A primes; the infinitude of safe primes would imply Conjecture A.
Artin's primitive root conjecture concerns primes p where a given integer is a primitive root, which depends on the factorization of p−1 — exactly the structure constrained by Form A.
Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions is the prototype result on prime distribution in structured sets; Erdős's question asks about a more restrictive structured set.

sections.title: Imports and Setup
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib prime basics, finite set infrastructure, natural number arithmetic, and tactic framework.

sections.title: Form Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsTwoTimePrimePlusOne (p = 2^k · q + 1) and IsTwoThreeTimePrimePlusOne (p = 2^k · 3^l · q + 1) predicates.

sections.title: Main Conjectures (OPEN)
sections.summary: States both variants of the infinitude conjecture as Set.Infinite axioms.

sections.title: Verified Examples and Non-Example
sections.summary: Computationally verified: 8 Form A primes ≤ 100 (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 29, 41, 97), one Form B-only example (61), and a non-example (37).

sections.title: Structural Theorems and Implications
sections.summary: Proves Form A ⊆ Form B, safe primes ⊆ Form A, smooth structure of p−1, and Conjecture A ⇒ Conjecture B.

sections.title: Computational Verification
sections.summary: Decidable check function for Form A membership and collective verification of all eight examples.

overview.historicalContext: This problem (Guy's B46) concerns the factorization structure of $p - 1$ for primes $p$. The study of $p - 1$ factorizations has deep roots: Artin's 1927 primitive root conjecture requires $p - 1$ to have large prime factors for a given integer to be a primitive root mod $p$. Conversely, Erdős asks about primes where $p - 1$ has very *few* prime factors — just a power of 2 and one other prime. The $k = 1$ case ($p = 2q + 1$) gives the safe primes, named for their use in cryptography (Diffie–Hellman, Schnorr groups). Hardy and Littlewood's Conjecture F (1923) predicts the density of prime pairs including safe primes: approximately $2C_2 x/(\log x)^2$ safe primes up to $x$, where $C_2 \approx 0.66$ is the twin primes constant. Pomerance's work on popular values of Euler's function further illuminated the structure of smooth-shifted primes.
overview.problemStatement: Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p = 2^k \cdot q + 1$ for some prime $q$ and $k \geq 0$? More generally, are there infinitely many primes $p = 2^k \cdot 3^l \cdot q + 1$?
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines both forms, states both infinitude conjectures as axioms, provides 8 computationally verified Form A examples and 1 Form B-only example, proves the logical hierarchy (safe primes ⇒ Conjecture A ⇒ Conjecture B), establishes the smooth structure of $p - 1$, and implements a decidable check function for computational exploration.
keyInsights: The $k = 1$ case is precisely the safe primes conjecture ($p = 2q + 1$), itself a major open problem connected to cryptographic security
Form A restricts $p - 1$ to have $\omega(p-1) \leq 2$ distinct prime factors; Form B allows $\omega(p-1) \leq 3$
The logical hierarchy is: infinitely many safe primes $\Rightarrow$ Conjecture A $\Rightarrow$ Conjecture B, each strictly weaker
$p = 61$ separates Form A from Form B: $60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ has three distinct prime factors, so 61 is Form B but not Form A
$p = 37$ satisfies neither form: $36 = 2^2 \cdot 3^2$ is $\{2,3\}$-smooth with no additional prime factor, showing the conditions are genuinely restrictive
The connection to Artin's primitive root conjecture arises because both problems concern the multiplicative structure of $p - 1$

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures both variants of Erdős Problem #1065, establishes their logical hierarchy, and provides extensive computational evidence. The $k = 1$ case connects to the safe primes conjecture, a cornerstone of modern cryptography. All structural theorems (Form A ⊆ Form B, smooth factorization, implication chain) are fully proved in Lean 4.
conclusion.implications: A resolution would illuminate the factorization structure of $p - 1$ for primes $p$, connecting to Artin's primitive root conjecture, the distribution of smooth numbers, and the security assumptions underlying Diffie–Hellman cryptography. Understanding when $p - 1$ can be nearly a prime power is fundamental to both analytic and computational number theory.
openQuestions: Are there infinitely many primes $p = 2^k \cdot q + 1$ (Conjecture A)?
Are there infinitely many safe primes $p = 2q + 1$? (Open, implies Conjecture A)
What is the density of Form A primes among all primes? Heuristics suggest positive lower density
Does allowing the factor $3^l$ in Form B significantly increase the density, or are most Form B primes already Form A?
